item.meaning: A phrase coined by Jawaharlal Nehru describing India's ability to maintain national cohesion amidst cultural plurality.
item.source_context: Chapter 8: Unity in Diversity, or 'Many in the One' (fees108.pdf)

item.title: Cultural Synthesis in Diversity
item.explanation: India's regional linguistic, culinary, and attire differences share deep underlying unity through epic narratives (Rāmāyaṇa, Pañchatantra) and agricultural festivals.
item.source_context: Chapter 8: Unity in Diversity, or 'Many in the One' (fees108.pdf)

item.name: Sri Aurobindo
item.role_or_contribution: Indian nationalist leader and philosopher who explained how individual inner nature (Swabhava) and duty (Swadharma) create social harmony.
item.source_context: Chapter 8: Unity in Diversity, or 'Many in the One' (fees108.pdf)

item.name: Rabindranath Tagore
item.role_or_contribution: Nobel laureate poet who composed India's national anthem, celebrating the geographic and cultural unity of India's diverse regions.
item.source_context: Chapter 8: Unity in Diversity, or 'Many in the One' (fees108.pdf)

item.description: The philosophical principle that personal inner nature (Swabhava) guides individual moral duty (Swadharma) for social harmony.
item.source_context: Chapter 8: Unity in Diversity, or 'Many in the One' (fees108.pdf)
